source: RFC 0007 §6.4 (review of 2026-11-21's merges, R3-9: availability of the shadow flow; maintainer's coordinator, 2026-11-21)
statement: An instance status that is listed and does not decode never fails the control plane's read of the statuses: its instance counts as live and acknowledging no window, so no shadow window passes on it and the change's answer names it in `waitingFor`, while every other status is read and `propagation` answers, counting it as recent and holding no document. Like a status that reads, it counts as live only for a minute after its instance's last write, which the life its key has left tells: each status is written with the key's exact life, an hour with no jitter (the readers' reach, `SNP-25`), so a key with less than that life minus a minute left was written more than a minute ago, whatever the reader's clock. It counts among the readers of the store (`CTL-89`) until its key expires. A value stored with no life counts only while its instance's entry in the list of instances is younger than its expiry. Each such status is logged with its instance and why, at most once a minute per instance, and counted (`cosec.control.shadow.status.unreadable`). A status under another instance's key, and a store that does not answer, still fail the read.
